clue.text: Duke, in a wood on hack, made a striking impression

indicators.note: on means the following group comes after the word for hack

parts.note: to hack is to cut

indicators.note: in puts the duke's letter inside a plus the wood

parts.note: ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A duke in a forest hacks away and makes a dramatic impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' looks like a verb acting on the wood, but it is just the first piece, with the rest placed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a dash is an idiom for looking stylish and impressive in public.

clue.text: Policeman arresting old criminal, hard lout

indicators.note: arresting means seizing, holding the pieces within the policeman

parts.note: a copper is a police officer

indicators.note: criminal means bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A policeman detains an elderly crook and a tough thug.
explanation.walkthrough: A copper is British slang for a police officer; 'criminal' is an adjective here, signalling a bent version of old.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, oafish person, a lout.

clue.text: Row across mouth of busy river

indicators.note: the row stretches across, surrounding the selected letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: a mouth is the opening, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of busy

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out where a bustling river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier of seats. The Tiber is the river through Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the Italian waterway flowing through Rome, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Talk about throwing contest, last in Olympics

parts.note: the discus is an athletics throwing event

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of Olympics

explanation.surface: Chatting about a discus event where the competitor came last at the Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss something is to talk it over, a straightforward synonym for the phrase.

clue.text: Son with girl getting on with a recreational activity

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a girl's name
boarding a bus or train is getting on it

explanation.surface: A boy gets along with a girl over a shared hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on with' suggests friendship, but 'getting on' is boarding and the rest is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Skateboarding is riding a small wheeled board for fun, an example of a pastime.

clue.text: A pair vandalised yard where bees are kept

indicators.note: vandalised things are smashed up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

parts.note: the letters of a pair, rearranged
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Two hooligans wrecked the yard where the hives stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is a place where beehives are set up, the beekeeper's equivalent of a farmyard.

clue.text: Couple bagging last of flour that is plain

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside, so the couple surrounds a letter

parts.note: a pair is a couple

indicators.note: only the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of flour
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Two people pack the remaining flour, which is nothing fancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as an adjective for the flour, but it is a noun: a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland in North America, a kind of open level land.

clue.text: I so rattle foreign philosopher

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are made unrecognisable by rearranging

parts.note: these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that they really unsettle a thinker from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek thinker, pupil of Plato, so an instance of the definition.

clue.text: Toy — headless one cartwheeled twice

indicators.note: a cartwheel turns over, so the letters are turned round
headless means losing the first letter
twice means the turned piece appears a second time

parts.note: one refers back to the toy named at the start

explanation.surface: A toy figure without its head turns two cartwheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' points back to the toy of the definition, so the toy word itself is the raw material, taken twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spool toy that spins down and climbs back up its string.

clue.text: Spherical object taken from conveyor belt

indicators.note: the letters are lifted straight out of the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A ball has been picked off a factory conveyor belt.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere or globe, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Football team in easy win? Acts otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: these eleven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A club expects a straightforward victory, but it plays out differently.
explanation.walkthrough: Swansea City is a Welsh club that has played in English football's leagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea City is a professional soccer club from South Wales, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Drop scone and alcoholic drink on landing? Sort of

parts.note: Scotch is whisky
a pancake landing is an aircraft dropping flat onto its belly

explanation.surface: A recipe question: a scone served with whisky on the stair landing?
explanation.walkthrough: A pancake landing is a flat crash-landing, hence 'sort of' landing. A drop scone is a small thick British pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is the British name for a small thick griddle cake, also called a Scotch pancake.

clue.text: Detective in our helicopter, squirming

indicators.note: squirming means wriggling about, so the letters writhe into a new order

parts.note: these thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An investigator is uncomfortable on board a helicopter with us.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth, an instance of the fictional investigator.

clue.text: Plan to once again consume a Carthusian liqueur

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
to reuse is to use up once more

explanation.surface: A scheme to drink a monks' liqueur all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: Carthusian means of the monastic order whose monks still make this green or yellow liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is the herbal liqueur distilled by Carthusian monks, named after their Grande Chartreuse monastery.

clue.text: Painter's picture's very good, after seeing that

indicators.note: one part placed after another means it is written later in the answer

parts.note: pic is short for picture
as means since, seeing that
so is an intensifier like very, as in 'so good'

explanation.surface: An admirer praises an artist's canvas after viewing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: 'very good' must yield just SO, the intensifier, placed after the word for 'seeing that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish artist who co-founded Cubism, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Miserable March — its second festival

indicators.note: something miserable is in a wretched state, so the letters are thrown into disarray

parts.note: the letters of march and its, rearranged
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A gloomy March brings the year's second celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the Christian celebration of the nativity of Jesus, an example of a feast day.

clue.text: Cat (he-cat) he shot

indicators.note: shot can mean ruined or worn out, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter fired at a big tom.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a spotted African big cat famed for speed, an example of the feline family.

clue.text: Previous title-holder, one meeting the Queen

parts.note: an earl holds a noble title
I is the Roman numeral one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A former champion is granted an audience with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previous title-holder' suggests a former champion, but the definition is 'Previous' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier as an adjective means prior or preceding in time, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Picture from one publication in the East

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mag is short for magazine
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A photograph taken from a single Far Eastern magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' looks like a noun but is the verb, to picture in the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine something is to form a mental image of it, i.e. to visualise.

clue.text: Accomplished European chemist

parts.note: accomplished things are done, in the past
Eur. is an abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A skilled scientist from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished' looks like 'skilful' but means finished, over and done.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French scientist behind pasteurisation, an example of a famous chemist.

clue.text: A kiss for a pound

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a loud smacking kiss
second meaning: British slang for one pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone offers a peck on the cheek in exchange for a quid.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are informal British slang; a quid is a pound coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word names both a noisy kiss and a single pound or dollar, so it fits each phrase.

clue.text: Railway official at Porthmadog, say, used to steam trains

indicators.note: used here means worked over or knocked about, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: these thirteen letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A railwayman in a Welsh heritage town once looked after steam engines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to' reads as 'formerly', but 'used' alone signals the shuffle and 'to' joins the letters. Porthmadog in Wales is home to steam railways.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationmaster runs a railway station, the official in charge at a stop such as Porthmadog.

clue.text: Note the manoeuvres demonstrating genuine power

parts.note: te is a note in tonic sol-fa, also spelt ti

indicators.note: manoeuvres means the letters of the are moved around

explanation.surface: A memo about the troop exercises showing real military might.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is followed by ETH, a rearrangement of THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or body with teeth has real force to enforce its will, an idiom for effective strength.

clue.text: A container, slightly open

parts.note: taken as written
a jar is a container

explanation.surface: A jar has its lid a little loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajar describes a door or lid left partly open, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Leaping in front of sailor pointing to a firework

indicators.note: being ahead means the first part is written before the second

parts.note: leaping is jumping
jack is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone bounds up to a seaman and points at a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumping jack is a small firecracker that hops about as it explodes, a type of pyrotechnic.

clue.text: Bird found in hedge, mutilated

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the following words, waiting to be found

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A bird was discovered in a hedge, badly injured.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian species, an example of the definition.

clue.text: A female in vehicle getting more reckless

indicators.note: in places a and the female inside the vehicle

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, a car
she is a female

explanation.surface: A woman in a car becomes a more dangerous driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The vehicle is a Rolls-Royce, known by its two-letter badge.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means hasty and heedless, so the comparative is more impetuous.

clue.text: Order changed for cashmere? I don't know

indicators.note: a changed order means the letters come in a different sequence

parts.note: these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper asks why the cashmere order was altered and is told nobody knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is a colloquial phrase for having no idea, equivalent to a shrug.
